# Control room "Quiet Light": design proposal v0.3

**Status:** PROPOSED, built on the v0.3 existing shell (scan-measured, photo-consistent at about ±0.1–0.2 m; Gate 1 revision under review). Every number below is generated by `model/monitoring_geometry.py` from the shell and the owner's tape measurements. The acoustician must review and on-site measurements must confirm it before anything is fabricated.

> ## v0.4 (8 Nov 2026, owner decision): FIRESIDE + CINEMA layout. This is the current starting point.
> - **Direction:** lengthwise on the building axis, facing the partition (unchanged), but the **console and both RL 901Ks are pulled into the room**.
>   - The listening position is at **0.375 L from the rear (gable) wall**: ears 3.08 m from the gable and 5.12 m from the partition.
>   - The speakers are 2.70 m from the partition.
>   - The stereo geometry is unchanged: 2.80 m apart, 2.80 m to the ears, ±30°.
> - **Existing wood stove kept in place.** The zone between the speakers and the partition becomes a **fireside lounge**: low, soft seating to the left of the stove, a non-combustible hearth pad, and the doorway route from the live room kept clear. The front-wall absorber stops about 0.9 m short of the stove.
> - **Family cinema:**
>   - A 3.0 m acoustically transparent 16:9 screen drops 0.25 m in front of the Geithains, with its bottom edge 1.2 m above the floor.
>   - A 3–4 seat sofa against the rear diffusers, plus two armchairs. From the sofa: 3.95 m to the screen, **42° wide, centre 14° above eye level**. The sightline clears the console meter bridge.
>   - The projector sits on the flat ceiling above the sofa (4.3 m throw, ratio 1.43).
>   - 5.1 now (the Geithains as L/R; a centre behind the screen, side surrounds and a sub), plus one-touch movie mode and blackout.
> - **Acoustic effect:**
>   - The front-wall SBIR notch moves from about 132 Hz to about 32 Hz, deep in the modal region and much less audible.
>   - The listening position at 0.375 L from the rear avoids the length-mode null at the room centre.
>   - The posts stay outside the stereo triangle.
>   - Keep the lounge furniture low and soft. Don't run the stove hard in long critical sessions.
> - **Moved:** the producer/outboard desk goes along the left wall (under the window line). Clients listen at the mix position.
> - Source of all numbers: `model/monitoring_geometry.json` (`layout: fireside`). Plan: `drawings/PR-102`. Renders: `renders/design/*_v04.png`.
>
> Sections 2–7 below describe the earlier v0.3 front-wall layout and are kept for reference. The table in section 3 is superseded by the v0.4 numbers above.

## 1. The room we actually have
| Measured fact | Value | Design consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Interior | 11.24 m wide × 8.20 m deep | Volume about 290 m³: generous for stereo, workable for 7.1.4 |
| Ceiling | asymmetric tray. Flat centre 4.11 m high and 3.54 m wide; slopes about 45°; low side zones 2.25 / 2.30 m, 2.58 / 2.00 m deep | The high flat strip is the natural acoustic and visual spine |
| Building axis | X = 5.88 m (entry door, clerestory, partition doorway and flat ceiling all on it); room mid-width is 5.62 | Listening axis goes on the building axis; side walls are 0.52 m asymmetric about it and must be equalised by treatment |
| Posts | one per side, X 2.58 / 9.24, about mid-depth (Y ≈ 4.25) | A transverse layout would put a post in the stereo field, so the room is used lengthwise |
| Openings | centred entry door, clerestory and two windows in the gable; four ribbon windows (sill 1.15, head 1.86); centred doorway in the partition | All kept. Windows stay as the "light" in Quiet Light, with acoustic shutters for control |
| Wood stove + flue | existing, near the partition, at about X 4.4 m — **exactly where the left RL 901K goes** | **Owner keeps the stove.** So either move it to the rear corner by the sofa (A1, recommended) or face the gable (B). Insurer/WETT inspection either way |

## 2. Orientation: decided by the evidence, alternatives quantified
| Option | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Lengthwise, facing the partition (recommended)** | ✅ | The front wall is interior (no glass, no exterior door behind the speakers). The entry door, clerestory and daylight end up behind the listener. The centred partition doorway sits **between** the speakers, so it is symmetric, stays usable as the route to the live room, and the screen covers it during screenings. The listening position falls at **37.5 % of the room length**. |
| B. Lengthwise, facing the gable | possible | Mirror image of A, with the same acoustics on paper. But windows, clerestory and the exterior door sit behind the speakers (glare on the screen, a leakier front wall), and clients arrive from the front of the room. |
| C. Transverse (facing a side wall) | ❌ | The posts at mid-depth fall on or near the listening axis inside the stereo triangle. The 2.58 / 2.00 m low zones are then front and back, making front-wall ceiling heights unequal. The ribbon windows end up directly behind the speakers or the listener. |

## 4. Acoustic screening (approximations, for the acoustician)
- **Axial modes (rectangular approximation):**
  - length: 20.9, 41.8, 62.8, 83.7 Hz
  - width: 15.3, 30.5, 45.8, 61.0 Hz
  - effective height (3.14 m): 54.6, 109 Hz
  - The asymmetric tray ceiling helps break up the height modes. The modal region is roughly below 60 Hz (Schroeder estimate).
- **Listening position at 0.375 L** avoids the length-mode pressure nulls at 0.25 L and 0.5 L.
- **Front-wall SBIR:** an omni quarter-wave estimate gives a first notch at about **132 Hz**. The RL 901K's cardioid bass reduces rear radiation, and a 300 mm broadband absorber covers the whole front wall. Final speaker distance gets tuned from measurements (stands on sliders ±0.2 m).
- **First reflections:**
  - Side walls are about 4.5 m from each speaker, so their reflections arrive late; the absorbers under the windows treat them.
  - The ceiling reflection point sits on the flat ceiling, so it gets an absorptive cloud of about 3.1 × 2.2 m at 3.9 m.
  - The console reflection is the classic one: tilt the meter bridge, and the speaker height and toe-in are set to keep the reflection behind the head.
- **Low frequencies:** use the two low side zones (2.2–2.3 m high, 2.0–2.6 m deep) for **deep LF trapping below the window sills** (about 0.75 m deep, full length). Their open volume above provides more. Bass management with two subs is for immersive mode.
- **Rear wall (gable), 5.1 m behind the listener:** diffusion made from **reclaimed Clark wood** (QRD-style slats) between the existing openings. The reflections arrive after about 30 ms, so diffusion rather than absorption.

No RT, isolation or frequency-response figures are claimed. These need the empty-room measurement and the acoustician.

- **Speakers:** compact coaxial monitors (model TBD; ideally a smaller Geithain for timbre matching) at an equal 2.8 m radius. Install conduit, rigging and blocking in phase 1.
- **Screen:**
  - A motorised **acoustically transparent 16:9 screen, 3.2 m wide**, drops in front of the Geithains for screening and retracts into a cassette on the flat ceiling. From the rear sofa it covers about 31° of view.
  - The screen bottom is at 0.80 m; viewing elevation from the mix position is about 14° to the screen centre.
  - Projector in a hush box on the flat ceiling at the rear (throw about 6.4 m).

## 6. Room fit-out (Quiet Light)
- **Floor:** pale oak over the existing floor, wool rug at the mix zone. *Confirm the existing floor build-up first:* it sits 0.35 m above the live slab and carries 2 × 48 kg monitors.
- **Light:**
  - Concealed dimmable **tunable-white LED coves along the two beam lines** wash the sloped planes and the flat ceiling. The tray ceiling becomes the light fixture, Turrell-like and with no visible luminaires.
  - Daylight comes through the existing windows, controlled by acoustic shutters.
  - Task lighting goes over the console only.
- **Materials:** lime-plaster-coloured fabric and plaster tones, dark fabric front wall, reclaimed walnut and Clark wood for diffusion, window benches and caps.
- **Seating:** mix chair, a producer/outboard desk behind the listening position (racks below), and a 2.8 m sofa against the rear diffusers. That is the client listening and screening row.
- **Machine room:** the middle-zone room next to the partition holds the computers, power amps and converters, keeping fan noise out of the control room. Tie-lines run through the partition at low level.
- **HVAC (indicative):**
  - Low-velocity linear slot supplies at the junctions of the flat ceiling and the slopes, fed from the roof void above the sloped ceiling (void inferred, see ledger X4). Low return at the rear.
  - The unit sits on isolators away from both rooms.
  - Noise criterion and design by a mechanical engineer.
- **Cable routes:**
  - Floor trench or raised plinth from the console to the machine room through the partition.
  - Ceiling raceways for the overhead speakers in the void.
  - Tie-lines to the live room run along the corridor.
